examples.ko: 이혼할 때 아이의 양육권을 누가 갖는지 정해야 해요.
examples.en: When parents divorce, they have to decide who gets custody of the child.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 양육권 문제로 오래 다퉜어요.
examples.en: The two of them argued for a long time over the custody issue.
The court granted custody to the mother.
Can the father also demand custody?
A custody lawsuit takes a long time.

examples.ko: 아이가 클 때까지 양육권은 엄마가 가지기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided that the mother would have custody until the child grows up.

explain: 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 '이혼', '친권', '소송'과 같이 자주 나와요. 보통 '양육권을 갖다', '양육권을 얻다', '양육권을 주장하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It often appears in news and legal talk together with words like '이혼' (divorce), '친권' (parental authority) and '소송' (lawsuit). It is usually used as '양육권을 갖다', '양육권을 얻다' or '양육권을 주장하다'.

en: choice between one and the other

examples.ko: 이번 문제는 양자택일이 아니라 둘 다 필요해요.
examples.en: This problem is not an either-or; we need both.

examples.ko: 시험에서 양자택일 문제는 찍어도 반은 맞아요.
examples.en: On an exam, you get half of the either-or questions right even if you guess.

examples.ko: 일과 가족 중 양자택일을 강요하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't force me to choose between work and family.
This is not a situation where we can choose just one of the two.

examples.ko: 둘 중 하나만 고르라는 양자택일로 보지 말고 천천히 생각해요.
examples.en: Don't see it as a choose-one-of-two matter; let's think slowly.
The company demanded that the employee choose one of the two.

explain: '양자택일을 강요하다', '양자택일의 문제'처럼 하나를 고르면 다른 하나는 포기해야 하는 상황에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '둘 중에 하나 골라'처럼 쉽게 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used as '양자택일을 강요하다' or '양자택일의 문제' when choosing one means giving up the other. In everyday talk people often say simply '둘 중에 하나 골라' (pick one of the two).

examples.en: I boiled the brisket for a long time to make the broth.
Please give me a geun of brisket at the butcher shop.
Seaweed soup tastes good with brisket in it.
Brisket goes well with soups and braised dishes.
I ate boiled brisket slices dipped in mustard.
At the seolleongtang restaurant, I ordered a soup with rice that had brisket in it.

explain: 소고기 부위 이름이에요. 줄여서 그냥 '양지'라고도 많이 말하고, 주로 국이나 수육을 만들 때 써요.
explain_en: It is the name of a beef cut. People often shorten it to just '양지', and it is mainly used for soups and boiled sliced beef (수육).

examples.ko: 우리 집 마당은 하루 종일 양지발라요.
examples.en: Our yard is sunny all day long.

examples.ko: 할머니는 양지바른 마루에 앉아 졸고 계세요.
examples.en: Grandmother is dozing on the sunny porch.

examples.ko: 양지바르고 조용한 동네로 이사 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move to a sunny, quiet neighborhood.
This room gets a lot of sun, so it's warm even in winter.
If the house is sunny, the potted plants grow well.

examples.ko: 고양이가 양지바른 담 밑에서 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is sleeping under the sunny wall.

explain: '양지바른 곳', '양지바른 마당'처럼 꾸미는 말로 가장 많이 써요. 반대는 해가 안 드는 '음지'예요. '바르다'가 르 불규칙이라 '양지발라요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is most often used to modify a noun, as in '양지바른 곳' or '양지바른 마당'. The opposite place is the shady '음지'. Because '바르다' is a 르-irregular verb, it becomes '양지발라요'.

examples.en: It is a house with a roof made of tin sheet.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 양철 지붕에서 소리가 커요.
examples.en: When it rains, the tin roof gets loud.
I packed kimchi in a tin lunch box.
I watered the plants with a tin watering can.
Tin sheet rusts when it gets old.

examples.ko: 시골 창고 문이 양철이라 바람에 덜컹거려요.
examples.en: The door of the country shed is tin, so it rattles in the wind.

explain: '양철 지붕', '양철통', '양철 대문'처럼 옛날 시골 풍경 이야기에 자주 나와요. 비 오는 날 '양철 지붕에 떨어지는 빗소리'처럼 소리와 함께 떠올리는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It often shows up in talk about old countryside scenes, as in '양철 지붕' (tin roof), '양철통' (tin bucket) or '양철 대문' (tin gate). People often link it with sound, like rain falling on a tin roof.

examples.en: I put rice and seasoned vegetables in a big bowl and mixed them.

examples.ko: 엄마가 양푼에 떡볶이를 가득 담아 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom filled a big bowl with tteokbokki for us.

examples.ko: 양푼 비빔밥은 숟가락으로 막 비벼 먹어야 맛있어요.
examples.en: Bibimbap in a big bowl tastes best when you mix it roughly with a spoon.
Where did our big bowl go?

examples.ko: 양푼 하나에 다섯 명이 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: Five of us ate together from one big bowl.
You can use a big bowl for a long time even if it gets dented.

explain: 음식을 담거나 비빌 때 쓰는 큰 그릇이에요. '양푼 비빔밥'처럼 여럿이 함께 먹는 편한 분위기와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a big bowl used for holding or mixing food. It fits the relaxed mood of eating together, as in '양푼 비빔밥'.

examples.en: I looked down on my opponent and lost badly.
Don't look down on me just because I'm young.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 사람들을 얕잡는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: That person has a habit of looking down on people.
They seem to have looked down on me because I'm new.
If you underestimate our team, you'll get burned.

examples.ko: 적을 얕잡으면 안 된다고 코치님이 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: The coach said we must not underestimate the opponent.

explain: 대부분 '얕잡아 보다' 형태로 써요. '얕보다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 상대의 힘이나 실력을 실제보다 낮게 보다가 낭패를 볼 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the form '얕잡아 보다'. It means almost the same as '얕보다'. It fits cases where you rate someone's strength or ability lower than it really is and then get caught out.

examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I walk with a waddle.
The bear lumbered toward the tree.

examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있었더니 다리가 아파서 어기적거려요.
examples.en: I sat for a long time and my legs hurt, so I'm walking stiffly.
The way the duck waddles is cute.
The child waddled around in big shoes.
Why are you walking so stiffly? Are you hurt?

explain: 몸이 무겁거나 다리가 불편해서 팔다리를 크게 움직이며 느리게 걷는 모습에 써요. 목적 없이 돌아다니는 '어슬렁거리다'와는 달리 걸음걸이가 둔하고 불편해 보일 때 말해요.
explain_en: It describes walking slowly with big, heavy movements because the body is heavy or the legs are uncomfortable. Unlike '어슬렁거리다' (to wander about aimlessly), it focuses on a clumsy, awkward gait.

examples.en: The bear lumbered off into the forest.
The child came waddling out.
My knee hurt, so I climbed the stairs stiffly.
The man came shambling toward the door.
The penguin waddles across the ice.
Stop dawdling along and come quickly!

explain: '걷다', '걸어가다', '올라가다' 같은 움직임 말 앞에서 주로 써요. 큰 몸이나 불편한 다리로 천천히 걷는 모습을 그릴 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used before movement verbs like '걷다', '걸어가다' and '올라가다'. It fits scenes of a big body or sore legs moving slowly.

examples.en: I danced with my shoulders while listening to the song.
When Dad is in a good mood, he starts moving his shoulders to a beat.
My shoulders start dancing on their own to the market music.
Grandfather sang while swaying his shoulders.
Even just moving your shoulders makes it feel lively.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 동생이 어깨춤을 추면서 방을 돌았어요.
examples.en: At the news of passing, my younger sibling went around the room dancing with shoulders swaying.

explain: 신이 나서 어깨를 들썩이며 추는 춤이에요. '어깨춤을 추다' 또는 '어깨춤이 나다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I felt like dancing when I heard about my promotion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁜 일이 있어서 몸이 저절로 들썩일 만큼 신이 날 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when something makes you so happy that you feel like dancing.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel like dancing for joy

explain_en: It is a dance where you bounce your shoulders in excitement. It is used as '어깨춤을 추다' or '어깨춤이 나다'.

en: as if (someone) wouldn't do it well; surely

examples.ko: 걱정하지 마세요, 민수가 어련히 알아서 할까요.
examples.en: Don't worry, Minsu will surely take care of it himself.

examples.ko: 어련히 잘 도착했겠죠. 전화 안 해도 돼요.
examples.en: I'm sure he arrived safely. You don't need to call.
Wouldn't the teacher surely handle the teaching well on their own?
I'm sure they've prepared well. Trust them and wait.
His parents must have decided it properly on their own.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 어련히 잘할까요? 왜 자꾸 확인해요?
examples.en: Of course he'll do it well, won't he? Why do you keep checking?

explain: '어련히 알아서 할까(요)?'처럼 '믿을 만하니 걱정할 필요 없다'는 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 말투에 따라 '그만 잔소리해요'라는 느낌도 날 수 있어서 윗사람에게는 조심해요.
explain_en: It is used as in '어련히 알아서 할까(요)?' to say that someone can be trusted so there's no need to worry. Depending on tone it can also sound like 'stop nagging', so be careful with people older than you.

examples.en: My mother's face keeps flickering before my eyes.
A shadow flickered outside the window and it startled me.
The moonlight is shimmering on the water.
I was sleepy and the letters in the book swam before my eyes.

examples.ko: 커튼 뒤에서 누가 어른거리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like someone is moving faintly behind the curtain.

examples.ko: 밤새 아이 모습이 눈에 어른거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The child's image kept haunting me all night, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 희미하게 보였다 안 보였다 하거나, 보고 싶은 사람의 모습이 자꾸 떠오를 때 써요. '아른거리다'와 비슷한 말이고, '눈앞에', '눈에'와 같이 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when something appears and disappears faintly, or when the image of someone you miss keeps coming to mind. '아른거리다' is a similar word, and it is often used with '눈앞에' or '눈에'.

examples.en: Heat haze shimmered up into the air.
The ripples glimmer on the water.

examples.ko: 불빛이 어른어른 보여서 가까이 가 봤어요.
examples.en: A light flickered faintly, so I went closer.

examples.ko: 더운 날 길 위로 열기가 어른어른 올라와요.
examples.en: On a hot day, heat shimmers up from the road.
The letters wavered in front of my eyes.
The shadows sway and flicker in the candlelight.

explain: 빛, 그림자, 열기처럼 흔들리며 희미하게 보이는 것 앞에 써요. '보이다', '흔들리다', '비치다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used before things that look faint and unsteady, like light, shadows or heat. It goes well with verbs like '보이다', '흔들리다' and '비치다'.

en: acting like a baby; child's act of coquetry

examples.en: The youngest still acts like a baby with Mom.

examples.ko: 어리광 그만 부리고 스스로 해 보세요.
examples.en: Stop acting spoiled and try doing it yourself.

examples.ko: 아픈 날에는 나도 어리광을 부리고 싶어요.
examples.en: On days when I'm sick, I want to act like a baby too.
I'm worried because my child is getting more and more clingy and spoiled.
He doesn't act like a baby in front of his younger sibling.
That kind of baby act doesn't work anymore.

explain: 거의 '어리광을 부리다'로 써요. '응석'과 비슷한데, 어른에게 '어리광 부리지 마'라고 하면 핀잔하는 말이 돼요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '어리광을 부리다'. It is similar to '응석', and telling an adult '어리광 부리지 마' is a scolding.

examples.ko: 첫 출근날 어리바리 헤매다가 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: On my first day at work, I wandered around in a daze and got lost.
Everyone goes around a bit lost when they're new.
I wasn't fully awake, so I answered in a daze.

examples.ko: 어리바리 서 있지 말고 이쪽으로 와요.
examples.en: Don't just stand there dazed; come over here.
On my first trip abroad, I wandered around feeling bewildered.

examples.ko: 그는 어리바리 앉아 있다가 버스를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: He sat there spaced out and missed the bus.

explain: 정신이 없고 서툴러 보이는 모습에 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. 친구나 동료끼리 편하게 말할 때 어울리고, 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is a colloquial word for looking dazed and clumsy. It suits casual talk between friends or coworkers, and is not used much in formal settings.

examples.en: I'm new, so I'm still a bit lost.
Your bumbling look was cute.
I'm always out of it in the morning, so I make mistakes.
It was my first time there, so I felt lost.
Don't act so spaced out.
The newbie who used to be lost now does the work well.

explain: 신입이나 낯선 곳에서 정신이 없고 서툰 사람에게 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 놀리는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a casual word for someone who is flustered and clumsy, like a newcomer in an unfamiliar place. It can sound teasing, so avoid using it about people older or higher than you.

examples.en: I got an award so suddenly that I was stunned.
I just woke up and I'm still groggy.
He looked at me with a bewildered face.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 소식에 한동안 어리벙벙해서 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was so stunned by the sudden news that I couldn't speak for a while.
Don't look so confused; try explaining slowly.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 들어 어리벙벙한 채로 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I took a wrong turn and stood there confused.

explain: 놀라거나 상황을 잘 몰라서 멍해진 상태예요. '어리둥절하다'와 비슷하고, 잠이 덜 깨서 정신이 흐릿할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes being dazed from surprise or not understanding a situation. It is similar to '어리둥절하다' and can also be used when you're groggy from sleep.

examples.en: It's impressive that the little one went on the errand all by herself.

examples.ko: 어린것을 두고 일하러 가려니 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to leave my little one and go to work.
What fault could those poor little ones have?
The little one doesn't know anything yet.
Grandmother took care of the little ones' meals first.
How can you yell at a little child like that?

explain: 어른이 아이를 안쓰럽거나 정겹게 여기며 부르는 말이고, 자기 자식을 낮춰 말할 때도 써요. 아이 앞에서 직접 부르면 얕보는 말로 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: Adults use it for a child they feel tender or sorry for, and also when speaking humbly about their own child. Calling a child this to their face can sound belittling.

examples.en: Don't guess; find out exactly.

examples.ko: 사람이 백 명쯤 온 것 같다고 어림짐작했어요.
examples.en: I roughly estimated that about a hundred people had come.
My rough guess wasn't far off.

examples.ko: 거리를 어림짐작해서 걸음 수를 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: I estimated the distance and counted my steps.
It's risky to decide things based only on guesswork.
Rough guesses often miss the mark.

explain: 정확한 계산이나 확인 없이 대충 헤아려 맞히는 것에 써요. '어림짐작으로', '어림짐작하다'처럼 쓰고, 정확하지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 중요한 결정에는 안 좋은 방법으로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for guessing roughly without exact calculation or checking. It appears as '어림짐작으로' or '어림짐작하다', and carries a sense of imprecision, so it is often mentioned as a poor basis for important decisions.

examples.en: At the circus, a clown handed out balloons.
The children laughed at the clown's funny gestures.
I dressed up like a clown and went to the party.

examples.ko: 그는 모임에서 늘 어릿광대 노릇을 해요.
examples.en: He always plays the clown at gatherings.

examples.ko: 어릿광대 옷을 입은 사람이 길에서 공연했어요.
examples.en: A person dressed as a clown performed on the street.

examples.ko: 나는 남을 웃기는 어릿광대로 살고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to live as a clown whose job is to make others laugh.

explain: 서커스나 놀이공원에서 사람들을 웃기는 사람을 가리켜요. '어릿광대 노릇을 하다'처럼 남을 웃기려고 일부러 바보 같은 역할을 하는 사람을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who makes people laugh at a circus or amusement park. It is also used figuratively, as in '어릿광대 노릇을 하다', for someone who deliberately plays the fool to amuse others.

examples.ko: 질문을 받자 그는 어물거리며 대답을 피했어요.
examples.en: When asked, he mumbled and avoided answering.
Don't mumble; say it clearly.

examples.ko: 입안에서 말이 어물거려서 알아들을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The words mumbled in his mouth, so I couldn't make them out.

examples.ko: 왜 자꾸 어물거려요? 하고 싶은 말이 뭐예요?
examples.en: Why do you keep hesitating? What do you want to say?
I dawdled from the morning and ended up late.
While he was dithering, the chance was gone.

explain: 말이나 행동을 분명하게 하지 않고 우물쭈물하거나 굼뜰 때 써요. 말에 쓰면 '얼버무리다', 행동에 쓰면 '꾸물거리다'와 느낌이 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone is vague or slow in speech or action. About speech it feels like '얼버무리다' (to mumble evasively), and about actions it feels like '꾸물거리다' (to dawdle).

examples.en: He trailed off, mumbling.
Don't answer vaguely; say it clearly.

examples.ko: 아침부터 어물어물 시간을 보내다 보니 벌써 점심이에요.
examples.en: I dawdled around since morning and now it's already lunchtime.
The child mumbled something vague and went into the room.
Don't try to slip out of it with a vague answer.

examples.ko: 할 말을 못 하고 어물어물 서 있기만 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't say what I wanted and just stood there fumbling.

explain: 말을 분명히 못 하고 얼버무리거나, 행동이 굼뜬 모습에 써요. '얼버무리다', '넘어가다', '대답하다'와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It describes mumbling without saying things clearly, or acting slowly. It often appears with verbs like '얼버무리다', '넘어가다' and '대답하다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 좀 어벙해 보여도 일은 잘해요.
examples.en: He may look a bit dopey, but he does his job well.

examples.ko: 어벙한 표정으로 서 있지 말고 도와줘요.
examples.en: Don't just stand there looking blank; help me.

examples.ko: 내 동생은 어벙해서 자주 물건을 잃어버려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a bit spacey and often loses things.
I acted spacey and made a mistake.
The friend who seemed goofy at first is now a team leader.
Why are you so out of it today?

explain: 조금 모자라거나 멍해 보이는 사람이나 행동을 편하게 말할 때 써요. 놀리는 느낌이 있어서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a casual word for someone or something that seems a bit dim or spaced out. It has a teasing tone, so avoid using it about people older than you or people you've just met.

examples.ko: 한 달에 십 킬로를 빼겠다는 건 어불성설이에요.
examples.en: Saying you'll lose ten kilos in a month is nonsense.
I think that makes no sense at all.
His story is so illogical that nobody believes it.

examples.ko: 어불성설 같은 주장은 받아들일 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't accept an argument that is so illogical.

examples.ko: 돈도 안 주고 일을 시키는 건 어불성설 아니에요?
examples.en: Isn't making someone work without pay absurd?
That plan sounds absurd to me.

explain: '~는 것은 어불성설이다'처럼 말이나 주장이 앞뒤가 안 맞고 이치에 어긋난다고 단호히 말할 때 써요. 토론이나 글에 어울리고, 일상 대화에서는 '말도 안 돼요'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used in patterns like '~는 것은 어불성설이다' to firmly say a statement or claim is illogical. It fits debates and writing, while in everyday talk people more often say '말도 안 돼요'.

examples.ko: 그는 어수룩해 보여서 물건을 비싸게 샀어요.
examples.en: He looked naive and ended up buying the item at a high price.
He acts naive, but he's actually very smart.

examples.ko: 시골에서 올라온 청년이 어수룩해서 길을 헤맸어요.
examples.en: The young man who came up from the countryside was green and got lost.
He may sound unpolished, but he has a warm heart.
The green newcomer now works well.
He seems to grant every request because he is so naive.

explain: 순진하고 세상일에 서툴러서 조금 허술해 보인다는 느낌이에요. '순진하다'가 마음이 깨끗하다는 쪽이라면 '어수룩하다'는 남에게 쉽게 속을 것 같은 모습을 말할 때 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It suggests someone who is simple and inexperienced in worldly matters, so they look a little careless. '순진하다' leans toward a pure heart, while '어수룩하다' fits someone who looks easy to fool.

examples.en: I went out for a walk as dusk fell.

examples.ko: 새벽 어스름 속에서 첫 버스가 왔어요.
examples.en: The first bus came in the dim light of dawn.
At twilight, the lights came on in house after house.

examples.ko: 저녁 어스름에 길이 잘 안 보여서 조심했어요.
examples.en: The road was hard to see in the evening dusk, so I was careful.
Someone was walking toward me in the half-light.
The train came in through the dim light.

explain: 해 질 무렵뿐 아니라 동트기 전에도 써서 '저녁 어스름', '새벽 어스름'처럼 말해요. '땅거미'는 저녁에만 쓴다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It can be used both at sunset and before sunrise, as in '저녁 어스름' and '새벽 어스름'. '땅거미' differs in that it is used for the evening only.

examples.en: The sky is dim now that the sun has set.
The room was dim, so I turned on the light.
I walked alone down the dimly lit alley.
The faint light of dawn came in through the window.
We played outside until it got dusky.
The mountain looked beautiful, faintly visible in the dim light.

explain: 완전히 깜깜하지 않고 빛이 희미하게 남은 상태에 써요. '어스름한 골목', '날이 어스름해지다'처럼 쓰고, 명사 '어스름'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It describes a state that is not completely dark, with faint light remaining. It is used as in '어스름한 골목' or '날이 어스름해지다', and it is good to learn it together with the noun '어스름'.
